question:
The weekly expenditure (in dollars) of 5 families on groceries is: Family A = 250, Family B = 400, Family C = 350, Family D = 500, Family E = 300.

Determine: (i) Average expenditure, (ii) Family spending above average, (iii) Difference between highest and lowest expenditure.

options.text: Average = $350, Families above average = B, D, Difference = $250
Average = $360, Families above average = B, D, Difference = $250
Average = $360, Families above average = C, D, Difference = $250
Average = $360, Families above average = B, D, Difference = $200

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the deviation method, assume the average is 350.

Deviations: A(−100), B(+50), C(0), D(+150), E(−50) → Sum of deviations = +50.

Actual Average = 350 + (50 ÷ 5) = 350 + 10 = $360.

Families spending more than the average ($360) are B ($400) and D ($500).

Difference = Highest (500) − Lowest (250) = $250.

**∴ The correct answer is Average = $360, Families above average = B, D, Difference = $250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weekly expenditure: Family A = $250, Family B = $400, Family C = $350, Family D = $500, Family E = $300.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee9d6698b18f6135a6d5fe80d7133f870f9524ea9b53027f79120328574b994b.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

Difference = Maximum value − Minimum value

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total expenditure = 250 + 400 + 350 + 500 + 300 = $1800

⇒ Average expenditure = 1800 ÷ 5 = $360

⇒ Comparing each family's expenditure with the calculated average ($360):

⇒ Family B ($400) and Family D ($500) spend more than the average.

⇒ Highest expenditure = $500 (Family D)

⇒ Lowest expenditure = $250 (Family A)

⇒ Difference = 500 − 250 = $250

**∴ The correct answer is Average = $360, Families above average = B, D, Difference = $250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average (Arithmetic Mean)

It represents the central value of a finite set of numbers, computed as the sum of the values divided by the number of values.

Deviation Method for Averages

Instead of adding large numbers, choose an assumed mean. Calculate the individual deviations, find their average, and add it back to the assumed mean to find the exact average.

Range

The range of a set of data is the difference between the highest and lowest values, indicating the overall spread of the data set.
